evidence.claim: DoorDash operates an online local commerce platform connecting merchants, consumers, and couriers, and its 2025 annual-report search result describes marketplace and commerce-platform offerings including white-label delivery fulfillment and merchant online-ordering tools.

Olo describes itself as a restaurant technology provider with ordering, payment, and guest-engagement solutions, trusted by more than 750 restaurant brands and connected to more than 400 integration partners.
Olo's 10-K search result says its platform integrates with POS systems, aggregators, delivery service providers, ordering service providers, payment processors, UX/UI providers, and loyalty programs.

PAR's annual-report search result states that it provides omnichannel cloud-based software and hardware to restaurants, including POS, customer engagement and loyalty, digital ordering and delivery, operational intelligence, payment processing, hardware, and related services.
PAR's 2025 annual-report search result says its omnichannel solutions are used in more than 150,000 active restaurant and retail locations globally.
Toast's 2025 annual-report search result describes digital ordering, online ordering and delivery, marketing, loyalty, POS, restaurant operations, and payments capabilities.

External context indicates Domino's built a competitive position around direct ordering, first-party customer data, commission-free unit economics, and customer habit of ordering directly rather than browsing third-party marketplaces.
External context indicates Domino's had more than 37 million loyalty members and used a DoorDash partnership to address a channel where it had been absent.
evidence.source_title: Deep Dive: Domino’s Pizza ($DPZ) - Rebound Capital

memory_update.text: OLO should be tracked as the purest small-cap public candidate for first-party restaurant ordering, delivery integration, payments, and guest-engagement infrastructure.
PAR should be tracked as an underfollowed restaurant operating-system candidate spanning POS, loyalty, digital ordering, delivery, payments, and operational intelligence.
The node is not only delivery marketplaces; it includes the control layer between restaurant customer demand, POS, loyalty databases, kitchen routing, payments, and delivery fulfillment.

Need later-layer verification of market caps, analyst coverage, customer concentration, module attach rates, payment volume, churn, and whether first-party ordering improves restaurant unit economics after software and delivery fees.

node: Delivery marketplaces, first-party ordering, loyalty, and customer-data infrastructure
summary: Expanded the direct public-company universe for restaurant digital distribution infrastructure. Two-lane result: DoorDash is the obvious marketplace reference anchor; Toast is a high-attention restaurant operating-system reference; Olo and PAR Technology are the underfollowed discovery candidates because their products sit closer to first-party ordering, order routing, loyalty, guest data, POS integration, and enterprise restaurant workflow control. The key Serenity question is whether restaurants increasingly pay for software that protects first-party customer relationships and reduces dependence on aggregator economics.
